2.web: “Oh that my anguish were weighed, and all my calamity laid in the balances!
2.asv: Oh that my vexation were but weighed, And all my calamity laid in the balances!

3.web: For now it would be heavier than the sand of the seas, therefore have my words been rash.
3.asv: For now it would be heavier than the sand of the seas: Therefore have my words been rash.

4.web: For the arrows of the Almighty are within me. My spirit drinks up their poison. The terrors of God set themselves in array against me.
4.asv: For the arrows of the Almighty are within me, The poison whereof my spirit drinketh up: The terrors of God do set themselves in array against me.

5.web: Does the wild donkey bray when he has grass? Or does the ox low over his fodder?
5.asv: Doth the wild ass bray when he hath grass? Or loweth the ox over his fodder?

6.web: Can that which has no flavor be eaten without salt? Or is there any taste in the white of an egg?
6.asv: Can that which hath no savor be eaten without salt? Or is there any taste in the white of an egg?

7.web: My soul refuses to touch them. They are as loathsome food to me.
7.asv: My soul refuseth to touch them; They are as loathsome food to me.

8.web: “Oh that I might have my request, that God would grant the thing that I long for,
8.asv: Oh that I might have my request; And that God would grantmethe thing that I long for!

9.web: even that it would please God to crush me; that he would let loose his hand, and cut me off!
9.asv: Even that it would please God to crush me; That he would let loose his hand, and cut me off!

10.web: Be it still my consolation, yes, let me exult in pain that doesn’t spare, that I have not denied the words of the Holy One.
10.asv: And be it still my consolation, Yea, let me exult in pain that spareth not, That I have not denied the words of the Holy One.

11.web: What is my strength, that I should wait? What is my end, that I should be patient?
11.asv: What is my strength, that I should wait? And what is mine end, that I should be patient?

12.web: Is my strength the strength of stones? Or is my flesh of brass?
12.asv: Is my strength the strength of stones? Or is my flesh of brass?

13.web: Isn’t it that I have no help in me, That wisdom is driven quite from me?
13.asv: Is it not that I have no help in me, And that wisdom is driven quite from me?

14.web: “To him who is ready to faint, kindness should be shown from his friend; even to him who forsakes the fear of the Almighty.
14.asv: To him that is ready to faint kindness should be showed from his friend; Even to him that forsaketh the fear of the Almighty.

15.web: My brothers have dealt deceitfully as a brook, as the channel of brooks that pass away;
15.asv: My brethren have dealt deceitfully as a brook, As the channel of brooks that pass away;

16.web: Which are black by reason of the ice, in which the snow hides itself.
16.asv: Which are black by reason of the ice, And wherein the snow hideth itself:

17.web: In the dry season, they vanish. When it is hot, they are consumed out of their place.
17.asv: What time they wax warm, they vanish; When it is hot, they are consumed out of their place.

18.web: The caravans that travel beside them turn aside. They go up into the waste, and perish.
18.asv: The caravansthat travelby the way of them turn aside; They go up into the waste, and perish.

19.web: The caravans of Tema looked. The companies of Sheba waited for them.
19.asv: The caravans of Tema looked, The companies of Sheba waited for them.

20.web: They were distressed because they were confident. They came there, and were confounded.
20.asv: They were put to shame because they had hoped; They came thither, and were confounded.

21.web: For now you are nothing. You see a terror, and are afraid.
21.asv: For now ye are nothing; Ye see a terror, and are afraid.

22.web: Did I say, ‘Give to me?’ or, ‘Offer a present for me from your substance?’
22.asv: Did I say, Give unto me? Or, Offer a present for me of your substance?

23.web: or, ‘Deliver me from the adversary’s hand?’ or, ‘Redeem me from the hand of the oppressors?’
23.asv: Or, Deliver me from the adversary’s hand? Or, Redeem me from the hand of the oppressors?

24.web: “Teach me, and I will hold my peace. Cause me to understand wherein I have erred.
24.asv: Teach me, and I will hold my peace; And cause me to understand wherein I have erred.

25.web: How forcible are words of uprightness! But your reproof, what does it reprove?
25.asv: How forcible are words of uprightness! But your reproof, what doth it reprove?

26.web: Do you intend to reprove words, since the speeches of one who is desperate are as wind?
26.asv: Do ye think to reprove words, Seeing that the speeches of one that is desperate are as wind?

27.web: Yes, you would even cast lots for the fatherless, and make merchandise of your friend.
27.asv: Yea, ye would castlotsupon the fatherless, And make merchandise of your friend.

28.web: Now therefore be pleased to look at me, for surely I shall not lie to your face.
28.asv: Now therefore be pleased to look upon me; For surely I shall not lie to your face.

29.web: Please return. Let there be no injustice. Yes, return again. My cause is righteous.
29.asv: Return, I pray you, let there be no injustice; Yea, return again, my cause is righteous.

30.web: Is there injustice on my tongue? Can’t my taste discern mischievous things?
30.asv: Is there injustice on my tongue? Cannot my taste discern mischievous things?
